{"decision": "APPLY", "workflow_yaml": "name: Test
on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]

jobs:
  test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    concurrency:
      group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}
      cancel-in-progress: true
    env:
      CI: true
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: lts/*
          cache: yarn
      - run: yarn install --immutable
      - run: yarn run playwright install --with-deps
      - run: yarn lint
      - run: yarn build # type check
      - run: yarn test
      - uses: codecov/codecov-action@v4
        with:
          token: ${{ secrets.CODECOV_TOKEN }}", "rationale": "The workflow runs on every push and pull request to main with no concurrency control, so repeated revisions on the same branch/PR can run in parallel and waste resources. Pattern P-LIT-CANCEL-STALE (stale_run_cancellation) supports cancelling superseded runs partitioned by workflow and branch/PR, with reported estimated VM-time savings (free 1.9%, paid 4.1%). Its preconditions are met: runs represent the same workflow and branch/PR, a newer revision supersedes older checks, and there is no release/deployment work. Using group ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }} isolates distinct branches/PRs, addressing the contraindication that distinct branches must not share a cancellation group. All existing steps (checkout, yarn install with existing yarn cache, playwright install, lint, build, test, codecov) are preserved unchanged, so build/test coverage and required checks are kept intact. P-LIT-GHA-CACHE is not applied because yarn dependency caching is already present via setup-node cache: yarn. A custom timeout (P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT) is not applied because there is no representative successful-duration history in ci_history and a fixed limit risks timing out valid slow playwright browser-install/test runs.", "evidence_ids": ["pattern:P-LIT-CANCEL-STALE"]}
